chift_routes.one_line: Native create through POST /companies.new: one Horus 'company' (third-party) record with IsCustomer=true, FolderId (resolved with the shared folder rule, D7) sent in the body. The connector must generate the required SearchKey (unique within the folder) and derive IsVatLiable, LanguageCode and CountryCode. It then reads the record back with GET /companies.info (Data.Folder.Id checked, D13) + POST /ibans.list + an account SearchKey lookup (cached accounts.list, or accounts.info with the same folder check), or possibly with one POST /companies.list call using Filter.Id + Include (A), and builds ClientItemOut with the shared Horus company → Chift partner mapper (D9). force_merge = companies.update + ibans.new on the existing supplier, after the same folder check. Only one flat address is kept. mobile, internal_notes, currency, the person fields, the company number of VAT-liable clients and non-IBAN bank accounts are lost, and is_company is always returned as true (D9).

summary: A Chift client is a Horus 'company', the single third-party record of a Horus folder, flagged IsCustomer/IsSupplier (Guide: Data model: "Companies are the legal entities a folder deals with: customers, suppliers and beneficiaries"). A Horus 'folder' corresponds to Chift's folder_id ("the accounting record of one company"), resolved with the shared folder rule (D7: required when the connection has several selected folders; otherwise the single selected folder, or the single folder visible through folders.list Mode 0). The primary call is POST /companies.new with FolderId in the JSON body. Of its 8 required fields, SearchKey, IsCustomer and IsSupplier have no Chift source. IsVatLiable is derived from vat. LanguageCode and CountryCode come from optional Chift data, with folder defaults as fallback (D9 write-side language fallback). Create calls "return only its identifier" (Guide: Responses & errors), so ClientItemOut needs a read-back: companies.info + ibans.list + account SearchKey resolution (two to three calls), or possibly one companies.list call with Filter.Id + Include (sideloading is supported on companies.list, but which include paths work is undocumented, A). The response is built with the shared Horus company → Chift partner mapper (D9) that get_invoices and create_invoice also use, and every Id-only Horus call is guarded by a Data.Folder.Id check (D13). With the optional pre-checks (duplicate VAT/ExternalReference, free SearchKey, account validation), one create costs about 3-7 calls. force_merge makes sense because Horus uses one object for both roles: companies.update {IsCustomer:true} (partial update, never "", with a proposed per-field merge policy, C6) plus ibans.new. Main risks: SearchKey generation (unique within the folder, but length/charset undocumented; the naming convention is a proposal for Chift, C8); duplicate VAT refused by default; a non-idempotent create, so no blind retry on 500/timeout despite the guide's generic backoff advice (duplicate protection is best-effort); a single flat address; several Chift fields with no writable Horus field (and is_company always read back as true); undocumented ErrorType values, pagination and rate limits.
verdict_rationale: The create itself is native. POST /companies.new covers name, VAT, contact data, one address, IBANs (inline), external reference and the receivable (concentration) account, and Horus has a single customer/supplier object, so force_merge maps cleanly to companies.update. Under the shared verdict calibration (D11: extra per-request calls such as read-backs, or the loss of fields clients rely on, make a route a workaround), the route is a 'workaround', for four reasons: (1) companies.new returns only {Id} (F: reference + Guide: Responses & errors), so ClientItemOut needs two to three extra read calls, each Id-only read carrying a folder check (D13); (2) a required Horus key (SearchKey) must be generated by the connector, and IsVatLiable/LanguageCode/CountryCode must be derived or defaulted; (3) the create is not idempotent (D), so retries need a best-effort check-before-retry pattern; (4) some Chift fields are lost or only emulated: secondary addresses, mobile, internal_notes, currency, first_name/last_name/function/company_id, company_number of VAT-liable clients, non-IBAN bank accounts, is_company (not persisted; always returned as true, D9) and active (only through the undocumented CustomerActivitySuspended, D9, A).

call_sequence: 0. Connection and conventions. consumer_id → stored connection record for one Horus license (api_url, access_token, refresh_token, expiry; Guide: Authentication overview, 'one record per connected license'). If expiry is a few minutes away, refresh through POST {api_url}/oauth2/access_token (grant_type=refresh_token) under a per-connection lock, and persist the new pair before using it, because refresh tokens are single-use. Every call: HTTPS to api_url, Authorization: Bearer, Content-Type: application/json, optional gzip. .info = GET with ?Id=; .list/.new/.update = POST with a JSON body. Deserialise responses tolerantly (ignore unknown properties, never rely on property order).

1. Resolve the folder (D7). folder_id given → FolderId; reject with 400 if it is not among the folders selected at Chift activation (Chift FolderItem.selected: "Requests targeting a folder that was not selected will be rejected"). folder_id absent → if exactly one folder was selected at activation, use it; if no selection is stored, POST /folders.list {Mode:0} (cached) and use the folder if exactly one is returned; otherwise (several selected or visible folders) reject with 400 'folder_id required'. GET /folders.info?Id=FolderId (cached) gives the Language and CountryCode defaults. Horus 403 → Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' with the Horus Details.

2. Local validation and transformation (before any Horus call; field-format failures → 422: vat, country, IBAN checksum, company_id if rejected; see the error_code row). Pick one address (proposed priority main > invoice > delivery, C3). Build Address = street + ' ' + number (+ '/' + box). Map country → uppercase alpha-2 CountryCode, checked against the cached countries.list (unknown → 422). Map language → LanguageCode (FR/NL/DE/EN/ES/PT, otherwise the folder Language, possibly 'XX': the D9 write-side fallback shared by every write route). Normalise vat (uppercase, strip spaces/dots/dashes; proposal, or reject with 422 per Chift decision); if malformed after cleaning → 422 ERROR_INVALID_VAT_FORMAT. IsVatLiable = vat present. Strip and uppercase the IBAN(s). Validate the IBAN checksum (failure → 422, proposal).

3. If account_number is given: look it up in the folder's cached accounts.list, or call POST /accounts.list {FolderId, Filter:{SearchKeys:[account_number]}} ('starts with' → keep the exact SearchKey match only). No match, or Inactive=true → 400. Never create accounts implicitly.

4a. If force_merge is set: GET /companies.info?Id={force_merge} and check Data.Folder.Id = FolderId (D13), or POST /companies.list {FolderId, Filter:{Id: force_merge}} (folder-scoped by its FolderId). Reject with 400 if it returns 404/empty, if Folder.Id ≠ FolderId, or if IsSupplier = false (proposal, C6; the alternative is a normal create). If IsCustomer is already true, skip the update and return 200 (proposal, C6). Otherwise POST /companies.update (Id-only call, sent only after the folder check) {CompanyId: force_merge, IsCustomer: true, CustomerConcentrationAccount (if given), CustomerActivitySuspended: true (if active=false), and, under the proposed fill-empty-fields policy (A, C6), each shared field (address block as a whole, ContactEmail, InvoiceEmail, PhoneNumber, Website, LanguageCode) only where the supplier's value is empty}. Every other field is null or omitted, never an empty string (an empty string erases data). ExternalReference is written only if the supplier has none; a different existing value is kept and a warning returned, and the merged client is then found by its Horus Id, not by external_reference. VatNumber is never written on a merge until Horus confirms how companies.update treats a duplicate VAT number (it has no AllowDuplicateVatNumber). The 200 response reflects the stored supplier data, not the request. Then POST /ibans.list {CompanyId}, and POST /ibans.new {FolderId, CompanyId, Iban} for each Chift IBAN not already present (omit IsDefault so the supplier's main IBAN is kept). Set Id = force_merge and go to step 7.

4b. Duplicate pre-check (normal path). Basis: Chift describes vat as unique per company and usable as a reliable identifier to match clients between systems. If vat: POST /companies.list {FolderId, Filter:{IsVatLiable:true, VatNumber}} (equals; several matches are possible when AllowDuplicateVatNumber was used: return all Ids, the IsCustomer match first). If external_reference: POST /companies.list {FolderId, Filter:{ExternalReference}}, keep exact matches only. Match with IsCustomer=true → 400 ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS (existing_code = Horus SearchKey/Id). Supplier-only match → 400 ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS whose message invites a retry with force_merge={Id}. Match that is beneficiary-only or has neither flag → 400 with the Id; never merge silently. Without vat and external_reference, no duplicate check runs (A, policy). Optional, if Chift enables it (C8): companies.list {FolderId, Filter:{Name}} with an exact post-filter, optionally with Email, returning a warning or ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS.

5. SearchKey: derive a candidate from name (uppercase, ASCII, A-Z0-9 only, truncated; prefix plus sequence when the result is shorter than 3 characters; proposed rule A, C8). POST /companies.list {FolderId, Filter:{SearchKey:candidate}} and post-filter for an exact match (search keys are 'unique within the folder'). On collision, append a numeric suffix and check again. This is a free-key check, not a duplicate check: a collision is treated as a homonym and the key gets a suffix (A, policy).

6. POST /companies.new {FolderId, SearchKey, Name, IsCustomer:true, IsSupplier:false, IsVatLiable, VatNumber?, AllowDuplicateVatNumber:false, LanguageCode, CountryCode, Address?, ZipCode?, Locality?, PhoneNumber?, Website?, ContactEmail?, InvoiceEmail?, ExternalReference?, CustomerConcentrationAccount?, CustomerActivitySuspended?, Ibans?:[{Iban, IsDefault:true, IsDomiciliation:false}]} → Id. Error handling: 400 → do not retry as-is. Log ErrorType/Details. Regenerate the SearchKey once only if ErrorType/Details points to a SearchKey conflict (ErrorType values undocumented). A duplicate VAT → 400 ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS. Anything else → Chift 400 with Details. 401 → refresh once and replay (the token was rejected, so the create was not processed, D); if the refresh fails, mark the connection disconnected. 403 → Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' with the Horus Details. 500, timeout or network error → do NOT apply the generic exponential-backoff retry blindly. First search companies.list by ExternalReference (exact), then VatNumber (equals), then the generated SearchKey (exact), and re-POST only if nothing is found (best-effort: the docs do not say whether a timed-out create can still commit after the search, or whether a new company is listed at once). When neither external_reference nor vat was sent, the generated SearchKey is the only key. It was free at step 5, so an exact match found now is treated as the company just created, and the flow continues with the read-back; a second company with a suffixed key is never posted after a timeout (D). Identical Create client calls in flight are serialised by a connector-side lock per (folder, VAT number, external_reference or sanitised name) (proposal, A).

7. Read-back. Documented path: GET /companies.info?Id={Id}, then check Data.Folder.Id = FolderId (D13). A mismatch should never happen because FolderId was sent on create; if it does, return 400 with the created Id in the error detail, log it, and never re-POST. The response gives all scalar fields, LastModifiedDate, SearchKey, MainIban, Ibans refs and the CustomerConcentrationAccount ref. Alternative to test (A): POST /companies.list {FolderId, Filter:{Id}, Include:"MainIban,Ibans,CustomerConcentrationAccount"} (folder-scoped by construction), resolving the refs from Included by Type then Id. That would replace steps 7-9 with one call.

8. POST /ibans.list {CompanyId: Id} → bank_accounts[] (is_primary = Data[].Id == MainIban.Id). ibans.list has no FolderId and returns no Folder, so its folder guard is the step-7 check on the company (D13). Skip when companies.info Data.Ibans is empty.

9. If Data.CustomerConcentrationAccount is not null: resolve its Id through the cached, folder-scoped accounts.list (Data[].Id → SearchKey), or call GET /accounts.info?Id=… and check Data.Folder.Id = FolderId (D13, else 400) → account_number. A value is expected even when account_number was omitted if Horus applies a default concentration account (D); otherwise account_number is null (?).

10. Build ClientItemOut from steps 7-9 with the shared Horus company → Chift partner mapper (D9): active = NOT CustomerActivitySuspended (A), true when absent; one 'main' address from Address (+Address2), ZipCode, Locality, CountryCode, with address-level phone/email = null; phone = ContactPhone; email = ContactEmail; is_company = true; language = lowercase Horus Language, 'XX' → null; third_party_account = company SearchKey; account_number = CustomerConcentrationAccount resolved to its SearchKey. The response is mapped from the read-back, not from the request. If companies.new succeeded but the read-back keeps failing, return the id and only the request values the connector wrote to Horus, mapped as D9 maps them (is_company = true, one 'main' address, fields Horus does not store = null), with last_updated_on = null and a warning; log the failure, retry the read later, and never re-POST.

Fallback when the sanitised name is empty or shorter than 3 characters: a prefix plus a sequence (A). Optional per-consumer schemes: use external_reference, or a prefix plus a sequence. A race between check and create can collide; regenerate only if the Horus 400 points to a SearchKey conflict. When create_invoice must create a partner from partner_info, the consumer's code is used as the SearchKey as sent (D10): in create_invoice, partner_info.account_number is looked up exactly as sent, never sanitised or truncated, and a code that breaks the Horus rules (H7) is rejected with 422.

horus_required_without_chift_source.label: F

horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: client_id/client_secret = Chift's registered Horus integration credentials. refresh_token = the stored token of the consumer's connection. grant_type = CONSTANT 'refresh_token'. Persist the returned pair before use.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: F

horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: CONSTANT false (the Horus default), so Horus refuses duplicates. Expose true only as an explicit connector setting.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: IsDefault=true on the IBAN from Chift iban (or on the first valid IBAN), false on the others. IsDomiciliation=false (Chift has no direct-debit mandate data). On ibans.new (merge path) omit IsDefault, so Horus sets it true only if the company has no IBAN yet.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

limitations.description: A Horus company has a single flat address (Address/Address2/ZipCode/Locality/CountryCode). The flat fields are documented; the absence of any address list or address type is deduced from the companies.new/update schemas as of the reference export (optional fields may be added without notice, Guide: Changes & versioning).
limitations.impact: Only one address is kept (proposed priority: main > invoice > delivery). The other addresses are lost, and Get clients will return one 'main' address.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: No Horus write field for mobile, internal_notes, function, first_name, last_name, company_id or currency (CurrencyCode is read-only on companies.info). Deduced from the absence of such fields in POST /companies.new / companies.update as of the reference export.
limitations.impact: These values are dropped and the response returns null for them; callers should not expect a round-trip.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: company_number has no write field. EnterpriseNumber is returned only when IsVatLiable=false.
limitations.impact: The enterprise number of a VAT-liable client is not stored separately. For non-VAT-liable clients it can be stored only if Horus confirms that VatNumber + IsVatLiable=false holds the enterprise number.
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: No company/individual flag and no active/inactive flag on companies; the only candidate is the undocumented CustomerActivitySuspended.
limitations.impact: is_company is not persisted: Create client and every later read return is_company=true (D9), so a client created as an individual (is_company=false) comes back as a company. active=false can be emulated only if Horus confirms the meaning of CustomerActivitySuspended (read as active = NOT CustomerActivitySuspended, D9).
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: Horus bank accounts are IBANs only (Iban + Bic); there is no local account number, routing code or currency per bank account (deduced from ibans.* and companies.new Ibans schemas).
limitations.impact: Non-IBAN bank_account values (US/CA/AU style) are lost. bank_accounts[].account_number/routing_code/currency are always null.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: companies.new returns only {Id} (reference RESPONSE 200, and Guide: Responses & errors: "Requests that create or update an entity return only its identifier").
limitations.impact: Two to three extra read calls are needed to return ClientItemOut: companies.info + ibans.list + an account lookup (cacheable), or possibly one companies.list call with Include (A). Latency, and exposure to undocumented rate limits, increase.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: SearchKey is required by Horus, has no Chift field, and must be unique within the folder (Guide: Data model).
limitations.impact: The connector must generate it and check for collisions per folder. Users may dislike generated codes (the convention is a proposal for Chift, C8), and the undocumented length/charset rules may cause 400s.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Duplicate VAT numbers are refused by default (AllowDuplicateVatNumber "False by default"; Guide: Managing customers & suppliers: "By default, a VAT number already used by another company is refused.").
limitations.impact: Creating a client whose VAT already exists (e.g. as a supplier) fails unless force_merge is used. A pre-check is needed to return ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS with the existing Id. The scope of the check (folder or license) and its ErrorType are '?'.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Most string filters use 'contains' (Guide: Making requests; companies.list Filter); accounts.list SearchKeys uses 'starts with'. Exact matching is documented only for VatNumber, Iban and CountryCodes (equals). Filter.Id is exact by construction on a full 36-character GUID (D).
limitations.impact: Duplicate, ExternalReference and SearchKey checks need client-side exact post-filtering.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Pagination, page size and rate limits are not documented in the API reference or the guides. Making requests covers naming, headers, filters, dates, partial updates and gzip only, and no list endpoint has page parameters.
limitations.impact: The connector assumes lists return every match (A); short SearchKey candidates may return large sets. Each Chift create costs about 3-7 calls with no known quota. Ask Horus (H5).

limitations.description: companies.new is not idempotent: the request schema has no idempotency key, and neither the reference nor the guides mention idempotency. The guide's generic '500 : retry later with exponential backoff' must therefore be overridden for this call.
limitations.impact: A blind retry after a 500, timeout or network error can create duplicate companies. The connector must search (ExternalReference → VatNumber → SearchKey) before re-posting. This is best-effort duplicate protection: the docs are silent on whether a timed-out create can commit after the search and on how soon a new company is listed, and two identical calls in flight need a connector-side lock (proposal).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: The ErrorType catalogue is not documented: only the envelope {ErrorType, Details, Message} and the example 'not_found' are.
limitations.impact: Horus 400s cannot be mapped reliably to specific Chift errors (duplicate VAT vs duplicate SearchKey vs invalid IBAN). The connector relies on its own pre-checks plus a generic 400 that carries Details.

limitations.description: Writes run against the license's real database (Guide: Testing the API), and no separate sandbox environment is documented. The 72-endpoint reference has no companies.delete (ibans.delete / ibans.clear exist).
limitations.impact: QA of Create client needs a dedicated test license or test folder from Horus. Test companies cannot be removed through the API (D); only their IBANs can.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Several Horus customer fields have no Chift source in ClientItemIn: CustomerPaymentDelay, UsualCustomerPaymentMode, domiciliation fields, ReminderEmail, Family, Name2, ContactPerson.
limitations.impact: They stay at Horus defaults. Payment terms must be managed elsewhere.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Horus Id-only calls (companies.info, accounts.info, ibans.list, ibans.info, companies.update) take a GUID without any FolderId, while one license connection can see several folders. companies.info and accounts.info return Data.Folder; ibans.list/ibans.info return no Folder, and companies.update returns only Id.
limitations.impact: Without a connector-side guard, a GUID from another folder of the same license could be read or updated. The connector checks Data.Folder.Id = FolderId on companies.info/accounts.info (400 otherwise) and calls ibans.* and companies.update only for a company that passed this check (D13).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: ClientItemOut is built with the shared Horus company → Chift partner mapper (D9), which exposes only ContactPhone/ContactEmail at root, one 'main' address, is_company = true and language with 'XX' → null.
limitations.impact: InvoiceEmail and ReminderEmail are not returned (a company with only an InvoiceEmail returns email = null), address-level phone/email are always null, and a folder-fallback language 'XX' written on create reads back as null.
limitations.label: D

edge_cases.case: vat already exists on a company with IsCustomer=true
edge_cases.handling: Pre-check via companies.list (VatNumber equals, IsVatLiable:true) and return 400 ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS with the existing SearchKey/Id (all Ids if several match, the customer first). Do not set AllowDuplicateVatNumber=true. Returning the existing client instead is a Chift policy decision.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: vat exists on a supplier-only company and force_merge is not set
edge_cases.handling: Horus would refuse the create (duplicate VAT). Return 400 ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS explaining that the third party exists as supplier {Id}, and suggest retrying with force_merge={Id}.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: VAT/ExternalReference match is a beneficiary-only record (IsBeneficiary=true) or has IsCustomer=false and IsSupplier=false
edge_cases.handling: Horus would still refuse the duplicate VAT. Return 400 with the existing Id and let the caller decide. Never merge silently: force_merge is defined for suppliers. Whether force_merge may target any existing company is a Chift policy question.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: force_merge Id not found, belongs to another folder, is not a supplier, or is already a customer
edge_cases.handling: 404 from companies.info (or an empty companies.list Filter.Id in FolderId) → 400 'unknown supplier'. Folder.Id ≠ FolderId → 400 (D13 cross-folder guard; companies.info takes only an Id). IsSupplier=false → 400. IsCustomer already true → no update needed; just return the read-back (idempotent). Both the 200 for an existing customer and the 400 for a non-supplier are proposals for Chift to confirm; the alternative for a non-supplier id is a normal create.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: force_merge target has no VatNumber, or a VatNumber different from the request vat
edge_cases.handling: Do not overwrite the VAT on the existing supplier. Reject with 400, or merge without touching VatNumber and warn, per Chift policy. A supplier without VAT number merged with a client that sends one stays non-VAT-liable until Horus confirms the duplicate-VAT behaviour of companies.update; the response shows vat = null, disclosed with a warning.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: force_merge update sends empty strings for missing Chift fields
edge_cases.handling: Forbidden: an empty non-null string erases the existing value (F, Guide: Making requests). Send null or omit every field that should not change. By default, set IsCustomer and the customer-specific fields, and fill shared fields only where the supplier's value is empty (proposal, C6).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: addresses[] is empty (allowed: no minItems in Chift) or contains several addresses of the same type
edge_cases.handling: Empty: no address fields; CountryCode from folders.info, so the read-back returns one main address holding only that country (D9). Several: take the first by the proposed priority main > invoice > delivery (C3) and warn about the dropped ones.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: language not in the Horus enum (e.g. 'it') or null
edge_cases.handling: Fall back to the folder Language (folders.info), sent as-is (possibly 'XX'), per the D9 write-side fallback shared by every write route. Do not reject, because LanguageCode is required. The read-back then returns the folder language, or null for 'XX' (D9), so the original language is not round-tripped.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: country given as alpha-3 ('BEL'), lowercase, or a VAT-style code ('EL' for Greece, 'UK')
edge_cases.handling: Normalise to uppercase ISO alpha-2 ('GR', 'GB') and check with countries.list; 422 if unknown. The EL/UK quirks come from general knowledge and need checking against the Horus country list.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Generated SearchKey collides with an existing company (or a concurrent create takes it between check and create)
edge_cases.handling: companies.list Filter.SearchKey (contains) + exact post-filter within the folder; append a numeric suffix until free. If companies.new still returns 400, regenerate and retry once only if ErrorType/Details points to a SearchKey conflict (ErrorType value to be confirmed with Horus). Otherwise surface the 400 with Details (guide: '400 : do not retry as-is'). A collision is a homonym, never ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: account_number does not exist in the folder, or is not a customer control account
edge_cases.handling: No exact match in accounts.list SearchKeys → 400 before calling companies.new. Whether a non-COLLECCUS account is accepted as CustomerConcentrationAccount is unknown.

edge_cases.case: account_number matches an account with Inactive=true
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 400 before companies.new (connector policy: an inactive control account should not receive new postings). Whether Horus itself would reject it is unknown.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: iban invalid, or iban equal to bank_account
edge_cases.handling: Strip spaces and validate the IBAN checksum before sending. Send one Ibans entry when both values are the same. Whether an invalid IBAN makes the whole companies.new fail is unknown. A checksum failure is rejected with 422 before companies.new (proposal).

edge_cases.case: iban already attached to another company in the folder
edge_cases.handling: Optional pre-check: companies.list {FolderId, Filter:{Iban}} (equals). If found, warn or reject per Chift policy. Whether Horus refuses duplicate IBANs is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: companies.new succeeds but the read-back (companies.info / ibans.list) fails or times out
edge_cases.handling: Do not re-POST (not idempotent). Retry the reads, which are safe; if they keep failing, return the id and only the request values the connector wrote to Horus, mapped as D9 maps them (is_company = true, one 'main' address, fields Horus does not store = null), with last_updated_on = null and a warning; log the failure, retry the read later, and never re-POST.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Timeout, network error or Horus 500 on companies.new (unknown outcome)
edge_cases.handling: Do NOT apply the guide's generic backoff retry blindly. First search companies.list by ExternalReference (exact), VatNumber (equals) or the generated SearchKey (exact). Re-POST only if nothing is found. This protection is best-effort: the docs do not say whether a timed-out create can still commit after the search, or whether a new company is listed at once. When neither external_reference nor vat was sent, the generated SearchKey is the only key. It was free at step 5, so an exact match found now is treated as the company just created, and the flow continues with the read-back; a second company with a suffixed key is never posted after a timeout (D). Identical Create client calls in flight are serialised by a connector-side lock per (folder, VAT number, external_reference or sanitised name) (proposal, A). After repeated 500s, return a Chift error and log endpoint + timestamp + body (the guide names developer@horus-software.be for persistent 500s).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Horus 401 on any call (token expired or revoked mid-sequence)
edge_cases.handling: Refresh once and replay the failed call. Replaying is safe even for companies.new, because a 401 means the token was rejected and the request was not processed (D). If the refresh fails, mark the connection disconnected and return an error asking for re-authorization.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Concurrent Create client calls for the same consumer while the access token is expiring
edge_cases.handling: Serialise token refresh per connection (lock or queue), persist the new token pair before use, and let the waiting calls reuse the new access token. Two parallel refreshes with the same single-use refresh token would make one of them fail.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: folder_id not visible to the connected Horus user (Horus 403)
edge_cases.handling: Map to Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)' with the Horus Details (D7). Folder visibility depends on the authorizing user's access (folders.list Mode 0 = all folders for accountants, accessible folders only for entrepreneurs).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: is_company=false with first_name/last_name and a name that differs
edge_cases.handling: Name = name (Chift required, minLength 1). first/last are dropped, optionally ContactPerson='first last'. Never use BeneficiaryInfo. The response returns is_company=true (D9), disclosed as data loss.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Same customer needed in several folders
edge_cases.handling: Companies belong to one folder (Guide: Data model tree: Folders → Companies; FolderId required on companies.new; companies.info returns Folder; search keys unique within the folder), so one company is created per folder. Chift ids are therefore folder-specific (D).
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Horus adds new properties to companies.info / ibans.list responses, or reorders them
edge_cases.handling: Deserialise tolerantly: ignore unknown properties, never rely on property order, and map unknown enum values (e.g. Language) to null.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: folder_id absent and the connection has several selected folders (or no stored selection and folders.list Mode 0 returns several folders)
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 400 'folder_id required' before any write (D7). With exactly one selected folder, or no selection and exactly one visible folder, use that folder.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: folder_id given but not among the folders selected at Chift activation
edge_cases.handling: Reject with 400 without calling Horus (Chift FolderItem.selected: "Requests targeting a folder that was not selected will be rejected"; D7).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: companies.info read-back (or accounts.info) returns a Data.Folder.Id different from FolderId
edge_cases.handling: D13: return 400 and log the Ids. For the read-back of a just-created company this should never happen (FolderId was sent on create); put the created Id in the error detail and never re-POST.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Created company has an InvoiceEmail but no ContactEmail (e.g. only an invoice-type address email was sent)
edge_cases.handling: D9 shared mapper: email = ContactEmail only, so response.email = null (no InvoiceEmail fallback, identical on every route).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: CustomerActivitySuspended is absent or null on the read-back
edge_cases.handling: D9 shared mapper: active = true. When present, active = NOT CustomerActivitySuspended; the meaning of the Horus flag is undocumented, so this stays an assumption until Horus confirms.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Client sent without vat and without external_reference
edge_cases.handling: No reliable duplicate check: a repeated call creates a second company with a suffixed search key. Optional, if Chift enables it: an exact-name check (optionally with e-mail) that returns a warning or ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS (C8).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: force_merge supplier already has a different ExternalReference
edge_cases.handling: Keep the supplier's ExternalReference, which the supplier-side system depends on, and return a warning; response.external_reference shows the stored value, and the merged client is looked up by its id. Overwriting or refusing are the alternatives for Chift (C6).
edge_cases.label: A

open_questions.question: Company SearchKey: what are the max length, the allowed characters and the case sensitivity? Does Horus generate a key when it is empty, and which ErrorType/Details does companies.new return for a duplicate SearchKey?
open_questions.why: SearchKey is required and has no Chift source. Uniqueness within the folder is documented; the rest is not, and a wrong generation rule causes 400s. (Consolidated as H7.)

open_questions.question: Which ErrorType values does companies.new return for validation failures: duplicate VAT, duplicate SearchKey, invalid IBAN, unknown or inactive concentration account, invalid LanguageCode/CountryCode?
open_questions.why: Turns generic Horus 400s into actionable Chift errors (e.g. ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS), decides when a SearchKey retry is allowed, and could make some pre-checks optional. (Consolidated as H6.)

open_questions.question: Is the duplicate-VAT check per folder or per license? Does Horus normalise VAT numbers (case, spaces, dots) before storing and comparing them?
open_questions.why: Drives the pre-check design: the equals pre-check misses a duplicate stored in another format. Companies belong to a folder, so a per-folder check is likely (D), but it is not stated. (Consolidated as H25.)

open_questions.question: Which LanguageCode values does companies.new accept, and what does 'XX' mean, given that the company enum lists both 'EN' and 'XX' and countries.list labels CountryNameXx as English?
open_questions.why: LanguageCode is required. Only the read/filter enum is documented, and the folder enum (FR/NL/DE/XX) has no EN. D9 sends the folder value as-is on write and returns 'XX' as null on read.

open_questions.question: Is CountryCode always ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (e.g. GR vs EL, GB vs UK)?
open_questions.why: Needed for a deterministic ISO → Horus transformation.

open_questions.question: How is a company's enterprise (local business) number written: VatNumber with IsVatLiable=false? Can it be stored for VAT-liable companies?
open_questions.why: Guide: Data model says companies are identified by 'a VAT number and/or a local business number', and companies.info returns EnterpriseNumber, but companies.new/update have no such field. (Consolidated as H11.)

open_questions.question: Can a company's CurrencyCode be set via the API?
open_questions.why: It is returned by companies.info but absent from companies.new/update.

open_questions.question: What does CustomerActivitySuspended mean, and is there an 'inactive' flag for companies?
open_questions.why: Needed to map Chift active: the shared mapper reads active = NOT CustomerActivitySuspended (D9) and stays an assumption until Horus confirms. (Consolidated as H11.)

open_questions.question: Is companies.new atomic with its Ibans array (an invalid IBAN means no company is created)? Are duplicate IBANs across companies refused?
open_questions.why: Decides whether to send IBANs inline or after creation via ibans.new, and whether an IBAN pre-check is needed. (Consolidated as H25.)

open_questions.question: Which CustomerConcentrationAccount is applied when it is omitted (folder setting? 400000?), must it be a collective (IntCategory COLLECCUS) account, and can a dedicated per-customer account created with accounts.new be used?
open_questions.why: The guide implies a default exists ('optional … set explicitly'). The answer defines the semantics of account_number, the validation rule, and whether accounts.new is ever needed. (Consolidated as H11.)

open_questions.question: What do Name2, Address2, Family and ContactPerson mean, and what are the field length limits?
open_questions.why: Needed to place box, address name, person names and long names without truncation. (Consolidated as H11.)

open_questions.question: Which relationship paths can be included on companies.list (MainIban, Ibans, CustomerConcentrationAccount), and which fields do the Included Ibans/Accounts entities carry (Iban/Bic? SearchKey?)?
open_questions.why: If supported, the read-back shrinks from two or three calls to one. (Consolidated as H15.)

open_questions.question: Do pagination, a maximum page size or rate limits apply to companies.list / accounts.list and per license?
open_questions.why: Neither the reference nor the guides mention them. They affect pre-check completeness and the call budget per create. (Consolidated as H5.)

open_questions.question: Can Horus provide a test license or test folder for connector QA, and can test companies be deleted (no companies.delete in the API)?
open_questions.why: Guide: Testing the API says requests run against the license's real database. (Consolidated as H17.)

open_questions.question: force_merge policy: on merge, which supplier fields may be overwritten with client data (name, address, contacts, VAT), or only IsCustomer and customer-specific fields? May force_merge target a beneficiary-only or flagless company? What should happen when the client's external_reference differs from the supplier's existing one (overwrite, keep with a warning, refuse)? Should an id that is not a supplier fall back to a normal create?
open_questions.why: companies.update overwrites what is sent. The business rule must match other Chift connectors. (Consolidated as C6.)

open_questions.question: On a duplicate VAT/external_reference, should the connector return 400 ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS or the existing client?
open_questions.why: The unified API should behave consistently across connectors. (Consolidated as C6.)

open_questions.question: Can the connector return warnings for dropped or non-round-tripped data (extra addresses, mobile, notes, currency, the company number of VAT-liable clients, is_company=false, which D9 always returns as true, and a language that falls back to the folder language)?
open_questions.why: Several fields are lost. D9 fixes is_company = true and 'XX' → null across routes, but callers still need a transparent contract. (Consolidated as C3.)

open_questions.question: How should the Horus third-party code (search key) of a new company be generated: from the name (proposed), from external_reference, a per-consumer prefix and sequence, or supplied by the consumer? When a client has neither vat nor external_reference and a company with the same name exists, should the connector create a second record, warn, or refuse?
open_questions.why: Accountants often have coding conventions for third-party codes (background). create_invoice uses partner_info.account_number as the search key as sent (D10), so a partner lookup finds only companies whose search key follows the same convention. (Consolidated as C8.)

open_questions.question: For a FolderId the user cannot access, or a company/account Id that belongs to another folder of the license, does Horus return 403, 404 or 400? Are Id-only calls (companies.info, ibans.list, companies.update) restricted to a folder server-side?
open_questions.why: D7 maps Horus 403 to Chift 400 'access denied for the connected Horus user (folder or action)', and D13 adds a connector-side Folder.Id check because the .info/.update calls take only a GUID. The answer confirms the error mapping and how much the guard protects. (Consolidated as H6.)

open_questions.question: Can a companies.new request that timed out on the client side still be committed afterwards? Is a new company returned by companies.list as soon as the create call has returned?
open_questions.why: The check-before-retry after a timeout or 500 is safe only if both hold; the docs give only the generic advice to retry 500s with exponential backoff. (Consolidated as H3.)

open_questions.question: Does companies.update refuse a VatNumber already used by another company? It has no AllowDuplicateVatNumber field.
open_questions.why: Decides whether a merge may write the client's VAT number onto a supplier without one. (Consolidated as H25.)

open_questions.question: Should a VAT number containing dots or spaces be normalised or rejected with ERROR_INVALID_VAT_FORMAT, as its message suggests? For validation errors without a predefined error_code (unknown country, invalid IBAN, unknown or inactive account), which status (400 or 422) and error_code do other connectors return?
open_questions.why: Chift’s examples use 422 for field formats and 400 for duplicates; the connector follows that split until Chift confirms. (Consolidated as C20.)

open_questions.question: Are companies.new PhoneNumber, Website and ContactPerson returned by companies.info as ContactPhone, ContactWebsite and ContactName? Is EnterpriseNumber ever returned for a VAT-liable company?
open_questions.why: The pairings are deduced from field names; they decide what the create response returns. (Consolidated as H25.)

open_questions.question: When several addresses are sent, which one becomes the single Horus address: main (proposed) or invoice? Is company_number = null acceptable for VAT-liable clients?
open_questions.why: Horus keeps one address per company and returns EnterpriseNumber only for non-VAT-liable companies. (Consolidated as C3.)

evidence_gaps: Pagination, maximum page size and rate limits are not documented in the API reference or the guides (Making requests covers naming, headers, filters, dates, partial updates and gzip only).
Company SearchKey: max length, allowed characters, case sensitivity and auto-generation when empty are not documented in the reference or the guides. Only 'unique within the folder' is stated.
No max length or pattern constraint on any companies.new string field in the reference or the guides.
The meaning of Name2, Address2, Family, ContactPerson (read back as ContactName) and CustomerActivitySuspended is not documented in the reference or the guides.
The default CustomerConcentrationAccount applied when it is omitted is not documented. Its existence is only implied by Guide: Managing customers & suppliers ('optional … set explicitly').
No write path for EnterpriseNumber (the local business number) is documented in the reference or the guides.
The LanguageCode values accepted on write are not documented (only the companies.list/info enum is), and neither is the meaning of 'XX'.
The CountryCode standard is not stated: alpha-2 is deduced from 'BE' examples, and countries.list is the only reference set.
The ErrorType catalogue is not documented: Guide: Responses & errors gives the envelope and the single example 'not_found'. There is no code for duplicate VAT, duplicate SearchKey or invalid IBAN.

Which relationship paths companies.list accepts in Include, and which fields the Included Ibans/Accounts entities carry, are not documented. Guide: Sideloading documents only the mechanism and the supported endpoints.
Atomicity of companies.new with its Ibans array, the behaviour on an invalid or duplicate IBAN, and the scope of the duplicate-VAT check (folder vs license) are not documented.
No idempotency mechanism (key or header) is documented for create calls.
Not provided at all: the Quickstart, Register your integration, Support & FAQ and Changelog pages, and the Postman collection, so announced changes to companies.* cannot be checked.

Whether Horus Id-only calls (companies.info, accounts.info, ibans.list, ibans.info, companies.update) are restricted to a folder server-side is not documented; they take only a GUID, hence the connector-side Data.Folder.Id guard (D13). ibans.list/ibans.info responses carry no Folder.
The HTTP status Horus returns for a FolderId the user cannot access (403 vs 404 vs 400) is not stated in the reference or the guides; the D7 error mapping assumes 403.
How Horus stores and compares VAT numbers (normalisation, case, separators) is undocumented, so the equals pre-check may miss a duplicate stored in another format.
ba_insights: Terminology trap: a Horus 'company' is NOT Chift's company/folder. It is a third party (customer, supplier and/or beneficiary) inside a Horus 'folder', the accounting dossier, which matches Chift's folder_id. Guide: Data model: 'A folder is the accounting record of one company' and 'Companies are the legal entities a folder deals with: customers, suppliers and beneficiaries'. companies.list also requires FolderId.

One object for both roles: IsCustomer and IsSupplier are two flags on the same record, so Chift's force_merge makes sense for Horus. It is implemented as companies.update {IsCustomer:true} on the existing supplier, not as a new record. This also explains why a VAT number already used by a supplier blocks a plain create ('By default, a VAT number already used by another company is refused').

Why multi-call: Horus create calls 'return only its identifier', but ClientItemOut needs last_updated_on (LastModifiedDate), third_party_account (SearchKey), bank_accounts[] (ibans.list) and account_number (a {Type, Id} reference resolved to a search key). That means two to three read calls per create (companies.info, ibans.list, the account lookup when not cached), about 3-7 calls in total with pre-checks, and possibly fewer if sideloading on companies.list covers IBANs and accounts (A). This is exactly the case's 'pull data from multiple endpoints' hint.

Read and write names appear to differ for the same data (deduced from the field names, to confirm with Horus): PhoneNumber/ContactPhone, Website/ContactWebsite, ContactPerson/ContactName, and CustomerConcentrationAccount (a search-key string on write, a {Type, Id} reference on read). Always map the response from the read-back, never from the request.

Account model: Horus uses a shared control (concentration) account, e.g. 400000 'Clients', and tracks the third party by its company. Evidence: customers.outstanding returns AccountSearchKey '400000' next to CompanySearchKey 'HORUS'; Guide: Bank… says customer lines (Type 1) carry 'Account': '400000' plus a required CompanyId; Guide: Outstanding items & matching says customer lines to match 'must belong to the same company'. So Chift account_number → CustomerConcentrationAccount, and third_party_account → company SearchKey. Do not confuse the two.

Required-field gap: of the 8 Horus-required fields, SearchKey, IsCustomer and IsSupplier have no Chift source. IsVatLiable is derived from vat. LanguageCode depends on an optional Chift field, CountryCode on an address array that may be empty, and FolderId on an optional query parameter. Explain to a client that the connector fills these by rule (constants, derivation, folder defaults), and that SearchKey generation is the main business-visible choice. The proposed default and its options are put to Chift (C8).

Search before create: Horus itself recommends ExternalReference as the key to 'find the company again reliably'. A pre-check by VAT (exact) and by external_reference ('contains' + exact post-filter) turns an opaque Horus 400 into Chift's standard ERROR_PARTNER_ALREADY_EXISTS (e.g. 'exists as supplier X, retry with force_merge'). The same search gives best-effort protection against duplicates when a create times out.

Reliability trap: the Horus guide's generic advice for 500 is 'retry later with exponential backoff', but companies.new is not idempotent. The connector must check-before-retry for 500s and timeouts; this is best-effort duplicate protection, not a guarantee. A 401 is different: the request was rejected, so refresh once and replay. This is the same check-before-retry rule as D12 on the invoice and misc-operation write routes.

Multi-tenant token hygiene: one Chift consumer = one Horus license connection (own api_url + tokens). Refresh tokens are single-use, so refreshes must be serialised per connection and the new pair persisted before use, or parallel Chift calls will break the connection.

IBANs: prefer the inline Ibans array in companies.new (one call, BIC auto-filled). ibans.new is only for an existing company (the force_merge path), because companies.update cannot change IBANs. The primary account is identified on read by comparing the ibans.list Id with companies.info MainIban.Id.

Data loss to disclose upfront: one address only; no mobile, notes, currency, person fields or non-IBAN accounts; the company number of VAT-liable clients; is_company not persisted (always returned as true, D9); active only via an unconfirmed field. This is why the verdict is 'workaround' (D11) even though the core create is native.
Never send empty strings on companies.update: Horus treats "" as 'erase' (Guide: Making requests, partial updates), so a careless merge would wipe the supplier's existing data.

Create client is a prerequisite for invoices: Guide: Posting sales & purchase invoices requires 'the CompanyId of the customer or supplier, found or created as described in Managing customers & suppliers'. A reliable response.id, with no duplicates, is therefore critical for the downstream invoice routes. create_invoice also reuses this route's required-field rules and its force_merge logic (companies.update setting the missing role flag, never ""; on invoice creation only as a Chift opt-in, the default being 422) when it must find or create the partner (D10), so these rules belong in one shared component. The search key differs: create_invoice uses the consumer's own code as sent, so reusing a company found under that code is legitimate there, whereas Create client derives the key from the name and treats a collision as a homonym.
Testing: writes hit the license's real database and companies cannot be deleted through the API, so Chift should ask Horus for a test license or folder before building QA for this route (H17).

One shared partner mapper (D9): Create client, get_invoices and create_invoice must return the same partner for the same Horus company: active = NOT CustomerActivitySuspended (A), one 'main' address, root phone/email (ContactPhone/ContactEmail), is_company = true, language lowercase with 'XX' → null, third_party_account = SearchKey, account_number = concentration account SearchKey. Implementing it once keeps the routes consistent and explains to a client why is_company=false or a language like 'it' does not round-trip.

Folder isolation is the connector's job (D13): Horus .info and .update calls take only a GUID, and one license connection can see several folders. So companies.info and accounts.info responses are checked on Data.Folder.Id before use, and the Id-only companies.update and ibans.* calls are made only for a company that passed this check.

folder_id (D7): optional in the Chift contract but "Required when the multiple folders feature is enabled". The connector uses the activation selection first and falls back to folders.list Mode 0 only when no selection is stored; anything ambiguous is a 400 'folder_id required', never a guess.
